source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 6 (i)-(ii): perpendicular pairs by dot product, parallel pairs by multiples / cross product (book p.283). Answer key PDF 312.

blocks.prompt: 6 (i) Which vectors, if any, are perpendicular or parallel: \(\underline{u} = 5\underline{i} - \underline{j} + \underline{k}\); \(\underline{v} = \underline{j} - 5\underline{k}\); \(\underline{w} = -15\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan teen vectors ke jore (pairs) check karne hain: kaun se perpendicular hain aur kaun se parallel.
Teen jore banenge: \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}\); \(\underline{u}, \underline{w}\); \(\underline{v}, \underline{w}\).
Plan: dot product zero to perpendicular; cross product zero (yani ek vector doosre ka multiple) to parallel.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{u} = 5\underline{i} - \underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{j} - 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = -15\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\).
Humein find karna hai: kaun se jore perpendicular hain aur kaun se parallel.
Tareeqa: Do non-zero vectors perpendicular tab hain jab un ka dot product 0 ho (14.2.6), kyunke \(\cos 90^{\circ} = 0\). Aur parallel tab hain jab un ka cross product \(\underline{0}\) ho (14.3.2), kyunke \(\sin 0^{\circ} = \sin 180^{\circ} = 0\); is ka matlab hai ek vector doosre ka koi multiple hai.

Teenon joron ke dot products
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = (5)(0) + (-1)(1) + (1)(-5)\]
\[= 0 - 1 - 5 = -6\]
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = (5)(-15) + (-1)(3) + (1)(-3)\]
\[= -75 - 3 - 3 = -81\]
\[\underline{v} \cdot \underline{w} = (0)(-15) + (1)(3) + (-5)(-3)\]
\[= 0 + 3 + 15 = 18\]
Kyun: Koi bhi dot product zero nahi aaya, is liye koi jora perpendicular nahi. \(\underline{v}\) mein \(\underline{i}\) nahi hai, yani us ka pehla component 0 hai; isay likhna mat bhooliye.

Kisi multiple ko pehchanein
\[\underline{w} = -15\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\]
\[= -3(5\underline{i} - \underline{j} + \underline{k}) = -3\underline{u}\]
Kyun: \(\underline{w}\) ke har component mein \(-3\) common hai; bahar nikalne par bracket mein bilkul \(\underline{u}\) bachta hai. Yani \(\underline{w}\) wohi line hai jis par \(\underline{u}\) hai, bas teen guna lambi aur ulti taraf.

Determinant likhein
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{w} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 5 & -1 & 1 \\ -15 & 3 & -3 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: Pehli row mein unit vectors \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\), doosri row mein pehle vector ke components \(\underline{u}\), teesri row mein doosre vector ke components \(\underline{w}\). Rows ki tarteeb wohi honi chahiye jo product ki tarteeb hai, warna jawab ka sign ulta ho jayega.

Teenon minors nikalein
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (-1)(-3) - (1)(3) = 0\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (5)(-3) - (1)(-15) = 0\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (5)(3) - (-1)(-15) = 0\]
Kyun: Har unit vector ki row aur column ko dhak dein (cover kar dein); jo 2 by 2 bachta hai us ka (upar baayan)(neeche daayan) minus (upar daayan)(neeche baayan) minor hai. Har product ko bracket mein likhne se negative signs ki ghalti nahi hoti.

Signs \(+, -, +\) lagayein
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{w} = \underline{i}(0) - \underline{j}(0) + \underline{k}(0)\]
\[= \underline{0}\]
Kyun: Determinant ko pehli row ke saath kholte waqt signs ka pattern \(+, -, +\) hota hai, yani beech wala \(\underline{j}\) ka term minus ho kar aata hai.
Dhyan dein: Sab se zyada ghalti isi beech wale minus mein hoti hai; \(-\underline{j}(\text{minor})\) mein minor khud negative ho to jawab plus ban jata hai.

Baaqi jore parallel nahi
\[\underline{u}, \underline{v}:\ \text{first components } 5, 0\]
\[\underline{v}, \underline{w}:\ \text{first components } 0, -15\]
Kyun: \(\underline{v}\) ka pehla component 0 hai jabke \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) ka nahi. Kisi bhi number ko 0 se multiply karein to 0 hi aata hai, is liye \(\underline{v}\) kisi ka multiple nahi ban sakta, na koi \(\underline{v}\) ka (kyunke \(\underline{v}\) ke baaqi components non-zero hain).
blocks.final_answer: Parallel: \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) (\(\underline{w} = -3\underline{u}\)). Perpendicular: koi jora nahi.

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) Which vectors, if any, are perpendicular or parallel: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}\); \(\underline{v} = -\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\); \(\underline{w} = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\underline{i} - \pi\underline{j} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Bilkul part (i) jaisa sawal, bas \(\underline{w}\) mein \(\pi\) aa gaya hai; ghabrana nahi, \(\pi\) bhi ek number hi hai.
Teen joron ka dot product dekhenge aur multiple dhoondenge.
Plan: teen dot products, phir common factor.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{u} = \underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = -\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = -\tfrac{\pi}{2}\underline{i} - \pi\underline{j} + \tfrac{\pi}{2}\underline{k}\).
Humein find karna hai: perpendicular aur parallel jore.
Tareeqa: Dot product zero to perpendicular; ek vector doosre ka multiple (cross product \(\underline{0}\)) to parallel. Wohi do qaide jo part (i) mein lagaye.

Teenon joron ke dot products
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = (1)(-1) + (2)(1) + (-1)(1)\]
\[= -1 + 2 - 1 = 0\]
\[\underline{v} \cdot \underline{w} = (-1)\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + (1)(-\pi) + (1)\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]
\[= \tfrac{\pi}{2} - \pi + \tfrac{\pi}{2} = 0\]
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = (1)\left(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + (2)(-\pi) + (-1)\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]
\[= -\tfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{2} = -3\pi\]
Kyun: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 0\) aur \(\underline{v} \cdot \underline{w} = 0\), yani yeh dono jore perpendicular hain. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{w} = -3\pi\) zero nahi, is liye \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{w}\) perpendicular nahi. \(\pi\) wale terms ko fractions ki tarah jama karein: \(\tfrac{\pi}{2} + \tfrac{\pi}{2} = \pi\).

Multiple dhoondein
\[\underline{w} = -\tfrac{\pi}{2}\underline{i} - \pi\underline{j} + \tfrac{\pi}{2}\underline{k}\]
\[= -\tfrac{\pi}{2}(\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}) = -\tfrac{\pi}{2}\,\underline{u}\]
Kyun: \(\underline{w}\) ke har component mein \(-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\) common hai: \(-\pi = -\tfrac{\pi}{2} \times 2\) aur \(\tfrac{\pi}{2} = -\tfrac{\pi}{2} \times (-1)\). Bracket mein bilkul \(\underline{u}\) bacha, is liye \(\underline{w}\) aur \(\underline{u}\) parallel hain.

Cross product se pakka karein
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{w} = -\tfrac{\pi}{2}(\underline{u} \times \underline{u})\]
\[= -\tfrac{\pi}{2}\,\underline{0} = \underline{0}\]
Kyun: Scalar (number) cross product se bahar aa jata hai, aur kisi vector ka apne aap se cross product hamesha zero hota hai, kyunke angle 0 hai aur \(\sin 0 = 0\).

Mantiq (logic) se tasdeeq
Kyun: \(\underline{v}\) to \(\underline{u}\) par perpendicular hai, aur \(\underline{w}\) bhi \(\underline{u}\) wali line par hi hai, to \(\underline{v}\) ko \(\underline{w}\) par bhi perpendicular hona chahiye; upar dot product zero aaya, baat mil gayi. \(\underline{u}\) aur \(\underline{v}\) parallel nahi ho sakte, kyunke do non-zero vectors ek saath perpendicular aur parallel nahi hote.
